site.name: Citymapper
site.framework: react (react-router SPA bundle /static/components/bundle-<hash>.js inside server-rendered Django pages; landing page is a separate React bundle; some routes are Next.js SSR)

summary: Citymapper's website is a public transit journey planner for 115 regions (252 cities) worldwide. Everything a visitor can do without an account goes through unsigned same-origin JSON calls under https://citymapper.com/api/<version>/: journey planning (transit, walk, cycle, cab and on-demand) between coordinates with depart-at or arrive-by times, live journey times, place search and autocomplete, nearby stops, stations, piers and bike docks per mode, stop details with live departures (bus, metro and rail feeds), line pages with stops, patterns and service status, region-wide line status with disruption texts, and line search. The city is always an explicit region_id parameter; the list of regions and cities, each region's modes, brands, bounding box and timezone are inlined into every server-rendered page as window.citymapper. A web account exists (sign in by e-mail magic link, Google or Facebook) and adds saved places (home, work, others), favourite stops and lines, and 'send to phone' saved journeys, all under /api/1/identity/. You are signed out on citymapper.com, so the account surface was mapped from the bundle and was not exercised; Citymapper Club and Pass payments are app-only. No request signing, nonce, captcha or bot challenge appeared; the site sits behind Cloudflare (__cf_bm) and served 200 to a separate CDP browser and to curl.

pages.purpose: Landing page: Get Me Somewhere form, city switcher, news teasers; fetches the current region's info and the brand directory
Journey planner shell: start and end search boxes, Now, Arrive, Leave time selector, map
Journey results: walk, cycle and cab summary row, Suggested and other sections of transit journeys with price, duration and live next departures
Journey detail: legs, stops, exits, live times; share and send-to-phone buttons
Shared trip link: resolves a slug to a journey signature, then shows the journey detail
Meet Me Somewhere link: destination card that plans a journey to a saved place
Meet Me Somewhere marketing page and place box that creates a go link
City home: journey form, account box, nearby mode tiles, lines card with status, Meet Me Somewhere box, strike map
All lines status for the region grouped by mode, with disruption details and partner status
Nearby list and map for one mode (stations, stops, docks, piers) around a point
Stop or station: routes, exits, live departures by platform or direction, nearby stops; favourite star
Line: branches (patterns), ordered stops, map path, status; favourite star and share
Brand-only journey planner for a partner network (journeys sent with partner=)
All cities; picking one writes the cm_region cookie and reloads
Sign up or log in: e-mail magic link, Facebook, Google
Terms of service and privacy policy documents
Server-rendered pages for shared ETAs, Citymapper Pass, payments authorisation and account e-mail flows; no caller in the web bundles

capabilities.name: Plan a transit journey
capabilities.user_action: Type a start and an end (or click the map), pick Now, Arrive or Leave, press GO
capabilities.notes: Inputs: start and end coordinates (names and addresses optional), region_id, departure_time or arrival_time as ISO UTC, step-free and microtransit flags. Returns sections (Suggested, others) and journeys with legs, live departure hints, price and duration. Exercised in NYC (now and arrive-by) and London (now), Paris (depart-at).

auth.mechanism: cookie-session (Django sessionid), optional; every public read works signed out
auth.csrf: A csrftoken cookie is set on first visit, but the bundle sends X-CSRFToken only on the uncalled city vote; identity writes send none (unknown whether the server enforces it)
auth.login_flow: E-mail magic link (POST identity/magiclink/create), Google Identity Services access token or Facebook SDK token posted to identity/sessions; no password form in the UI; no Apple sign-in
auth.refresh: none observed; a signed-out session answers 403 on identity/user_data

pagination.terminator: one response per query; a later window is a new query with a later departure_time
the response is the next departures window (about 30 to 60 minutes); the UI re-polls every 30 s
single snapshot; the UI refetches every 2 minutes
single snapshot; the UI refetches every 10 s (bundle)
fewer than limit elements, or move the location; no offset or cursor exists

caveats.detail: Cloudflare fronts the site and sets __cf_bm. No challenge appeared for your browser, a separate CDP Brave profile or plain curl; behaviour at higher rates is untested.
caveats.evidence: response headers server: cloudflare, cf-ray, set-cookie __cf_bm (curl and CDP captures 2026-10-10)

caveats.detail: No rate-limit headers (x-ratelimit-*, retry-after) on any API response; thresholds unknown. Pace at 3 s or more per request.
caveats.evidence: response headers in var/captures/run-2026-10-10-082844-*.jsonl list only cf-cache-status and x-version

caveats.detail: No request signing or nonce. The journey 'signature' is a JSON journey descriptor returned by the planner; /trip/signature?signature= carries it pako-deflated and base64 encoded.
caveats.evidence: journeys[].signature is a 900-character JSON string; bundle route table (research/bundle/api-inventory.md)

caveats.detail: Identity writes (places, favourites, saved journeys) send no CSRF header from the web client; whether the server enforces csrftoken is unknown until a signed-in write is tried.

Web account exists but you are signed out on citymapper.com, and signing in may create an account (magic link, Google or Facebook). Account reads and writes cannot be verified until you sign in yourself.
caveats.evidence: GET /api/1/identity/user_data 403 in your browser; login dialog shows e-mail, Facebook, Google

caveats.detail: Citymapper Club and Pass are paid features; Pass payment methods live on turnstile-api.citymapper.com and need a Session-Id the web pages never expose. App-only on the web.
caveats.evidence: bundle turnstile methods with no caller; news posts on Club features

caveats.detail: Share and Meet Me Somewhere links (createtripurl, createshorturl) are GET requests that create public URLs; they are writes visible to others.
caveats.evidence: bundle create-links.js; trip-share.js calls it on mount of the share block

caveats.detail: 8 regions have api_enabled false (fr-nantes, fr-bordeaux, fr-toulouse, fr-strasbourg, fr-marseille, ch-ch, mc-monaco, at-vienna); routing there may be absent or partial. Coordinates outside a region's bounding box are rejected client side as out of bounds.
caveats.evidence: window.citymapper.regions in the /nyc HTML; journey-results toggleOutOfBounds

caveats.detail: No websockets or SSE. Live data is polled: departures and journey times every 30 s, line status every 2 minutes, vehicles every 10 s.
caveats.evidence: CDP captures report 0 websocket frames; bundle timers

caveats.detail: Region config and the city list exist only inside 2 to 15 MB server-rendered HTML pages (or /resource/region-info per region); reading the city list costs one large page load, so it should be cached.
caveats.evidence: city-paris 4.8 MB, nearby-paris-metro 15 MB, city-london 8 MB in capture logs

caveats.detail: Embedded Google Maps browser key (39 characters) and Google and Facebook client ids in the bundle; only used for map tiles and social sign-in, never needed by the program.
caveats.evidence: bundle constants GOOGLE_MAPS_API_KEY, GOOGLE_KEY, FACEBOOK_APP_ID (names and lengths only)

caveats.detail: This is the website's private API, not the official developer API; the terms of service link is /api/1/resources?id=citymapper-terms-of-service.
Bike docks have no detail page (404); dock availability comes from nearby results only.
The web client's delete-place call passes placeId where place_id is required, so the web UI cannot remove a saved place; the program must send place_id itself.

open_questions: Account surface (user_data, places, favourites, saved journeys, update_user) is mapped from the bundle only: response shapes and CSRF enforcement need one signed-in session, which only you can create.
vehiclelocations was not fired on any line page walked (live_availability 0 on NYC 6, M15, London Bakerloo); which regions have live vehicles is unknown.

refreshjourneys, gettrip, getshorturl, eta, placeresolve, geocode, schedules, routepaths, everythingmap, weather, transitscore, traveltime, vehiclehire, walk v1 and blog are defined in the bundle but were not observed live; the engineer stage replays them once each.
Response bodies of findtransport were not captured (seen by URL in your browser only).
How far ahead departure_time may be set, and whether past times are accepted, is untested.
Brand planner pages (/{region}/planner/{brand}) were not visited; valid brand slugs are unknown.
